7.	The word X comes from the ancient Greek verb meaning "to pant." It was first used as a medical term by Hippocrates in the 5th century BCE. For most of medical history, it was treated with everything from menthol cigarettes (which don’t work) to strong coffee (which contains theophylline, a mild bronchodilator that actually helps). The first effective treatment was developed in the 1950s by a pharmacist's daughter who noticed that her sister found relief from a perfume atomizer, leading directly to the development of the pressurized metered-dose Y that is still in use today.
